fixture_name: Six HAWK pedestrian crossings — US final design (FHWA case study, PD)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Nighttime conspicuity of a HAWK display at an arterial pedestrian crossing is a substantive final-design-stage safety issue directly affecting drivers' stop decisions while pedestrians are in the crossing.
justifications.evidence_grounding: The verbatim quote in EV-US-001 ('Drivers may be confused by competing background visual elements at night') directly supports the pivotal claim and matches the cited Tucson case-study issue.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a safety_concern with no normative/compliance claim conflated in; conspicuity concern and any compliance matters remain categorically distinct.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Retroreflective border on the signal backplate is a specific, actionable, FHWA-recognized low-cost countermeasure targeted at exactly the recorded night-confusion problem.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians are explicitly identified as the exposed road users should drivers misread or detect the display late, tying driver conspicuity to VRU protection.

justifications.substance: Short pedestrian clearance intervals leaving elderly walkers exposed when conflicting releases begin is a substantive, scheme-specific safety issue at the corridor's highest pedestrian/bicycle collision sites.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal claim is supported by a verbatim quote from EV-US-016 ('The pedestrian clearance interval may be short, particularly for elderly pedestrians'), tied to these exact sites via the recorded TABLE A.10 Issue 2 reference.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a safety_concern rather than a compliance question under FHWA final-design RSA semantics; verifying walking-speed assumptions behind signal timing is stage-appropriate and categories stay distinct.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Recommendation is specific and actionable: reprogramme clearance intervals at all six named HAWK crossings using a reduced assumed walking speed, a viable final-design-stage action.
justifications.vru_coverage: VRU impacts are the explicit focus of the finding: pedestrians and elderly pedestrians are named in road_users and the scenario centers on their clearance exposure.
